anomalies.measured: 2026-11-19, the 66 recordings of the apartment scene (simulator). Head: 160107 walking samples (a forward command) of 63 runs; the pose is each joint's median over the runs' medians; a sample within 0.10 rad of it in 81 %, over 0.30 rad from it in 12 %; episodes of 1 s or more over 0.30 rad: 209 in 20 runs, and 1 each in b9 r2, b10b r1 and b11 r1, 2 in b10b r2 (over 0.20 rad: 8 and 9 in b10b r1 and r2). Streams: the longest gap between state samples 1.40 s and between depth frames 1.41 s, except apartment-1117c (25 s). Refusals for no room to turn: 123 of 240 had a nearest return of 280 mm or more, and the map was more than 5 cm tighter than the truth in 25 of those 123 against 19 of the other 117 (it does not separate). No-path refusals with a free start, a goal that is not lethal and nothing within 0.30 m of the pose by the cost map: 8 of 181, in 2 runs (b10b r1, b12 r2)
anomalies.why: the thresholds of the robot-tagged anomalies that are the duck's (RFC-0019 step 1, PHASE3-PREP B1): the head's walking pose and how far from it counts as off (a glance that left the head pitched tilted the odometry), how long the state and depth streams may be silent before they are stale (3 s is more than twice the longest gap of a running run), the sensor's clear distance at which a refusal for no room to turn disagrees with the map, and the distance round the pose inside which something in the map explains a refusal. Measured in the simulator only; the real duck has its own measurement to make (its walking head pose is robotd's default, neck 13 deg and head 20 deg, SIDE-DROPS.md)

odometry.measured: 2026-11-14, robots/duck/sim/probes/odom_vs_truth.py (straight walks, 3 x 8 s per speed, truth = body server trunk) and robots/duck/sim/odom_scale.py over ~41 m of navigation logs (0.909)
odometry.why: robotd's odometry reads ~10 % long in the simulator and mapd builds its map from it; the navigator scales odometry, mapd's poses and mapd's grid by this factor (operator, 2026-11-14: options 2 and 3). A real duck gets its own measurement (phase 5). Remove when robotd or mapd corrects it upstream.

pivot.measured: 2026-11-16. A turn on the spot creeps the way the duck faces: 0.27 m per full turn, p95 0.54 m, from the truth over the challenge course (robots/duck/sim/probes/turn_drift.py). robots/duck/sim/probes/pivot_counter.py, ch5-s3, a half turn to the right at 0.8 rad/s, one sample each: moved 0.111 m with vx 0, 0.058 m with -0.035, 0.026 m with -0.06.
pivot.why: a U-turn in a 60 cm corridor (challenge 5) ended 8-11 cm toward the side it turned to and was refused for no room to turn: 6/10 with vx 0. With -0.06 sent during a pivot: 10/10, twice; challenges 1, 3, 8, 9 10/10, challenge 2 9/10 (seed 5 stalled after a detour that began before any pivot; 3/3 on a rerun). A side-choice before a large turn (from the map, then from a head glance) was tried first: 6/10 and 3/10, dropped. The real duck pivots backward by upstream (RFC-0008 §4) and keeps 0 until its pivot is measured.

mount.measured: 2026-11-16. Range: the simulator's tof.py casts unit rays (mj_ray) and reports the hit distance along each, so readings are radial. Pitch: robots/duck/sim/probes/floor_fit.py over the challenge course's 40 flat-floor runs, the offset (0 to 4 deg in 0.5 deg steps with radial readings, and the real duck's 3 deg axial) that puts the recorded floor returns at floor height; 2.5 deg radial places them at +5.5 to -3.7 mm from 0.3 to 0.9 m (mean |error| 2.8 mm, the smallest), 0 deg radial 16 to 32 mm high (23.2), 3 deg axial 6 to 18 mm low (14.6). The servo joints alone (tof_truth.py, which leaves the model's passive backlash hinges at 0) put the optical axis 3.0 deg less steep than 3 deg believed: the extra ~2.5 deg is not in the servo angles, most likely the head sagging on its backlash hinges (not measured directly).
mount.why: with the real duck's values (3 deg, axial) the cliff check placed the floor up to 2 cm too low and, with the head near level (the walk's first second, the neck pitched up ~13 deg), stopped for drops that were not there: 131 frames and 8 cliff stops in the challenge course's 40 runs on flat floor (robots/duck/sim/probes/cliff_replay.py). 0 deg also removed them but by placing the floor too high, which made the check blind to the first 2-3 cm of any drop. The real duck keeps mapd's 3 deg and axial ranges (cliff.py's defaults); whether the real sensor's ranges are axial is not checked here.
